title: The Past, And Where You Were
label: ch:hi-atit
canDo: I can say where I was and what I used to do, put the sentence in the negative, and use the postposition that pins a person to a place.

payoff.summary: Ask where somebody was and answer for yourself, using the exact sentence the first practice paper prints as reading item 14 and moving it one step into the past.
payoff.note: Closes two points. HI-A1-V-12 said nothing in the corpus was past-tense at all, and that Hindi needs at minimum tha to say where one was or what one used to do -- the chapter supplies tha, thi and the, the negative, and the past habitual, which is the present habitual the track has taught since chapter 5 with its final word swapped. HI-A1-POST-05 is named in the inventory as turning two mock items: par had never been introduced as a word, only carried inside the chapter-94 phrase ham station par milenge, where it was a lump. The chapter also pays down script debt: the letter tha had never been taught anywhere in the track, which is why no past-tense lesson could be written before now, and HI-S126-letter-tha teaches it.
